file_name: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.txt

barriers.description: Severe time and staffing constraints forced the usability consultants to work at high speed with only two consultants, compressing the UCD process into an eight-week window and very fast iterations.
barriers.justification: The limited time and staffing reduced the team's capacity to conduct thorough iterative cycles, evaluate designs, and deepen user understanding, hindering integrate feedback & iteration, evaluate designs, and manage user understanding workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The project group had worked for five months nailing down the organizational requirements and their time was running out. They planned to prepare and anchor the results of the project in the organisation through a review process before the end of the year. Therefore the UCD process could not take more than eight weeks. ... However, the project was important and prestigious for the usability company and it was judged that we would be able to deliver on time by working with two consultants on top speed.

barriers.description: Project-group members only participated intermittently and attendance at interviews and exercises was limited (e.g., only one PPG member allowed per interview), and consultants worked largely outside the procurer's offices.
barriers.justification: Restricted and infrequent stakeholder participation limited designers' ability to facilitate stakeholder involvement, build shared understanding, and coordinate multidisciplinary collaboration, undermining manage user understanding and coordinate multidisciplinary team workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Although they were active and engaged, the members of the PPG, on the other hand, only participated occasionally in the hands-on work, such as on an interview or in a design session and then got the results presented to them in a weekly workshop. ... In order to not interfere too much with the actual interviews only one member of the PPG was allowed to attend on each interview session. ... they comment that they should have participated more in the activities and that all work should have been done in their offices, instead of having the usability consultants work in their own office.

barriers.description: Organizational requirements provided by the procurer were high-level and insufficiently detailed, and the PPG failed to further concretize them to the level of the user requirements.
barriers.justification: The lack of actionable, detailed organizational requirements prevented designers from aligning and integrating business constraints with user-driven design decisions, hindering manage user understanding, specify user requirements, and integrate feedback & iteration workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We identified the organizational requirements first and they did not reach the same level of concretization as the users’ requirements. (...) In retrospect it becomes clear that the halt was necessary not only for the PPG to understand the user requirements, but also to specify and secure the organizational requirements. The PPG had not been able to detail these to the level that the user requirements were specified.

barriers.description: A project halt was initiated by the procurement project leader when the PPG felt uncertain and unable to argue design decisions, interrupting the planned iterative work.
barriers.justification: The stakeholder decision to stop work mid-second iteration directly disrupted designers' ability to continue iteration and evaluation, delaying integration of findings and further prototyping, thus hindering integrate feedback & iteration and evaluate designs workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, a few days into the second iteration the procurement project leader called us to announce that the project needed to make a halt. The PPG had not been able to follow and understand all the decisions that had been taken during the design process.
